newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran hangs two for spying, economic sabotage.
newsitem.headline: Iran hangs two for spying, economic sabotage.

text.p: Iran has hanged two men for spying for Israel and the CIA and committing economic sabotage during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war, newspapers reported on Sunday.
They said the two Iranians were hanged at Tehran's Qasr prison on January 1 after their death sentences were upheld by the Supreme Court in December.

Hedayatollah Zendehdel, a Jewish businessmen who converted to Islam, and businessman Abolqassem Majd-Abkahi, were sentenced to death in July on charges including leading a network of 150 people involved in economic fraud during the 1980-88 war and leaking classified military information to enemies.
A third man, former air forcer officer Abdolreza Yazdanshenas, had also been sentenced to death on similar charges, but the newspapers only reported the execution of the other two.
Iranian press reports had said they worked for Israel and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).
Three other men linked to the network received jail sentences in July ranging from seven to 23 years.
